data.title: Household Sound Safari: Hunt for Letter Sounds!
data.subject: Language Arts
data.topic: Phonics: Letter-Sound Group 2 (c, k, e, h, r, m, d)
data.overview: Grab an explorer basket and set off on an indoor scavenger hunt! Young learners will search around their home for everyday items that begin with target letter sounds, strengthening phonemic awareness through active, multi-sensory discovery.
learningObjectives: Identify and articulate the beginning sound for target consonants and vowels (c, k, e, h, r, m, d).
Match physical household objects to their corresponding initial letter cards.
Isolate beginning phonemes accurately without adding a trailing vowel sound (e.g., saying crisp /m/ instead of /muh/).

steps.title: Make Your Sound Cards
steps.instruction: Help your child write one target letter clearly on each paper square using lower-case letters: c, k, e, h, r, m, d.
steps.tip: Write 'c' and 'k' together on one card if desired, since they make the same hard /k/ sound in words like cup and key.

steps.title: Warm Up Explorer Ears
steps.instruction: Hold up each letter card and practice saying its clean sound together. Make the sound short and bouncy (like /d/ for duck, /h/ like breathing out hot air, and /e/ like in egg).
steps.scienceNote: Keeping sounds crisp without adding 'uh' at the end (saying /d/ instead of /duh/) makes it much easier for early readers to blend sounds together into words later.
steps.tip: Press lips together for /m/ and hum gently so your child can feel the vibration on their lips.

steps.title: Begin the Safari Hunt
steps.instruction: Hand your child the collection basket. Walk through one or two rooms together to search for safe items that start with each letter sound (for example, a hat for /h/, a marker for /m/, or a cup for /c/).

checkpoint.question: Can you count how many objects you gathered in your safari basket?

steps.tip: If stuck on the short vowel /e/, look in the kitchen fridge for an egg, an envelope on the desk, or an elephant toy.

steps.title: Unpack and Match
steps.instruction: Spread the letter cards out on the floor or sorting tray. Pull one treasure out of the basket at a time, name it clearly, and set it next to the card with its matching starting sound.

checkpoint.question: Does the first sound in your item's name match the letter card you set it next to?

steps.title: Sound Safari Quick Grab
steps.instruction: Leave the matched pairs on display. The caregiver calls out a letter sound (such as /r/), and the child runs or reaches to gently touch the item and card that make that sound (like the ribbon).

checkpoint.question: Which letter sounds felt easiest to hear at the start of words, and which ones felt trickier?

reflectionPrompts.question: Say the word 'mat' and then 'hat'. What happens to your mouth and sound when you change the first letter?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Isolate beginning phonemes accurately without adding a trailing vowel sound.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Notice how your lips close tight for /m/ but stay open for a puff of breath on /h/.

reflectionPrompts.question: Why do you think the letters 'c' and 'k' can both match items like a cup and a key?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Match physical household objects to their corresponding initial letter cards.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Say 'cat' and 'kite'. What sound do you hear at the very beginning of both?

reflectionPrompts.question: Look around your bedroom right now. What is one object you see, and what letter sound does its name start with?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Identify and articulate the beginning sound for target consonants and vowels.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think of items like a door, a rug, or a pillow.

documentationPrompt.instruction: Take a photo of your child's completed sound museum, showing each household item placed next to its handmade letter card.
documentationPrompt.suggestedCaption: Our sound safari found [number] treasures! My favorite match was [item name] for the letter sound /[letter]/. #SoundSafari #EarlyPhonics

extensions.title: Secret Sound Detective
extensions.description: Place three objects on the mat where two share the same starting sound and one does not (e.g., ring, ribbon, cup). Have the child identify the imposter item that has a different sound.

safetyNotes: Adult helper recommended: Walk alongside your child to guide them toward safe areas and ensure breakable items are not touched.
Avoid small objects that could pose a choking hazard for younger siblings nearby.
Remind explorers to use walking feet indoors during the scavenger hunt.

problems.question: Which one starts with the c sound?
problems.rationale: Cat begins with the c sound. Sun begins with the s sound, and ant begins with the a sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have students place their hand by their mouth and make the /k/ sound to feel the burst of air when saying cat.
successCriteria: Identify the initial hard sound of the letter c in familiar spoken words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.statement: The letter k and the letter c make the same sound like cat and kite.
problems.rationale: Both the letter 'c' and the letter 'k' can make the hard /k/ sound at the beginning of words like 'cat' and 'kite'. Even though they look different, they share this important sound in Letter-Sound Group 2.
problems.teachingNote: Help students practice making the crisp /k/ sound using the back of their throat, and point out that different letters can sometimes make the exact same sound in English words.
successCriteria: Recognize that the letter c and the letter k share the same hard sound
Associate the letters c and k with initial vocabulary words like cat and kite
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with big H and little h?
problems.rationale: The word hat begins with the /h/ sound made by both big H and little h. Dog begins with the letter D, and ring begins with the letter R. Both uppercase H and lowercase h make the same starting sound in hat.
problems.teachingNote: Remind learners that uppercase H and lowercase h share the same breathy /h/ sound even though they look different.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /h/ sound associated with uppercase H and lowercase h
Distinguish the beginning sound of hat from other familiar words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the short e sound?
problems.rationale: Egg begins with the short e sound, making the 'eh' sound at the start. Hat begins with the 'h' sound and dog begins with the 'd' sound. Listening to the first sound helps identify egg as the correct match.
problems.teachingNote: Have children practice making the 'eh' sound by mimicking cracking open an egg. Emphasize hearing the initial vowel sound compared to starting consonant sounds.
successCriteria: Identify words that begin with the short e sound
Distinguish initial letter sounds in spoken words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which animal starts with a Group 2 letter sound?
problems.rationale: Dog begins with the /d/ sound, which is part of our Group 2 letters. Snake begins with /s/ and pig begins with /p/, which are both from Group 1. Listening to the first sound in dog helps us know it belongs in Group 2!
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce the initial /d/ sound by asking students to tap their tongues behind their teeth, contrasting it with the /s/ hiss and /p/ lip-pop from Group 1.
successCriteria: Distinguish between Group 1 (s, a, t, i, p, n) and Group 2 (c, k, e, h, r, m, d) letter sounds
Identify the beginning sound of a spoken word
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which one starts with the 'h' sound?
problems.rationale: Hat begins with the 'h' sound, made by puffing out a gentle breath. Pen starts with the 'p' sound, and map starts with the 'm' sound.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to hold their hand in front of their mouth to feel the gentle puff of air when saying the /h/ sound.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /h/ sound in familiar spoken words.

objectives.objective:
Letter-Sound Group 2: c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**New Sounds Introduced:**
/k/, /ĕ/, /h/, /r/, /m/, /d/

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d

**Focus:** Introduce the new sounds while systematically reviewing the sounds from Group 1. Practice problems must pull from the full 13-letter cumulative list. Note: 'c' and 'k' are introduced together as they make the same primary sound.
objectives.notes: Direct letter-sound identification omits 'r' from Group 2, and none of the cumulative review letters (s, a, t, i, p, n) receive letter-sound assessment opportunities.

objectives.objective: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme. Assess without first saying its sound: s, a, t, i, p, n, c, k, e, h, r, m, d.
objectives.notes: Oral sound production is only assessed for 4 letters (m, n, e, s). Missing production for c, k, h, r, d, a, t, i, and p. Remaining blocks substitute receptive recognition.

detectedConstraints.description: Generator reported residual unaskableLetters=['t','p','c','k','h','d'] prevented oral sound production testing on stop consonants in di-letter-sounds.
Fast-fact and knowledge-check use tap-based keyword picture recognition, which fails to assess independent oral phoneme production.

coverage.summary: While the lesson introduces the Group 2 sounds, neither objective provides sufficient evidence of cumulative mastery. Letter-sound identification (obj1) fails to assess 'r' and all Group 1 review letters. Sound production (obj2) only assesses oral production for 4 continuous sounds due to unaskable letter constraints on stop consonants, with the remaining review blocks reverting to off-target receptive recognition tasks.
